## PM claim + dispatch order — R19, **measure first; the fix shape depends on what you find**

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), round **R19**, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-6138-fields-schema-block-parity`.

### Why this card matters more than its size

`#5867`'s batches 1 and 3 moved these blocks into the compile population and I **accepted them on counts that read stronger than they were**. A self-declared interface with no imports type-checks no matter what it says. So "N blocks now compile" was true and "N blocks are now checked against the shipped types" was not — and this card family has been reporting the first while implying the second. Correcting that is the point here.

### ⚠️ Step 1 is a measurement, and it may change the fix

The card offers **A** (annotate against the exported type) and **B** (keep the interface, add a parity checker), and says neither is safe to guess. It also raises a third possibility that is not either of them:

> `value`, `className` and `disabled` are plausibly **widget props** (`FieldWidgetComponentProps`), not field *metadata*.

⛔ **Do not choose between A and B before establishing two facts:**

1. **The divergence across all 26 pages.** Only 2 were measured. For each page, the documented `*FieldSchema` key set versus the correspondingly-named exported `*FieldMetadata` (plus `BaseFieldMetadata`). Report it as a table.
2. **Whether the extra keys are `FieldWidgetComponentProps` members.** Read the shipped type and say so, per key.

**If the extra keys turn out to be widget props, STOP and report before implementing.** That would mean the pages merge two different shapes under one "Field Schema" heading — a structural documentation defect whose fix is to separate them, which is neither A nor B. Guessing A there would delete keys that are legitimately documented, just filed under the wrong heading.

### The ruling, conditional on that measurement

**If the divergence is plain drift (the extra keys belong to no shipped type): take A.** Replace the self-declared interface with a literal annotated against the exported `*FieldMetadata`, so the gate pins the documented shape to the shipped one.

The reason A over B: B adds a checker whose job is to keep a **second source of truth** honest, while A **removes the second source of truth**. Contract-first (AGENTS.md #0.1) prefers deleting the duplicate over instrumenting it. And this session has already refused three times to mint something so documentation becomes retroactively true — B is the mirror of that: building machinery so a divergent copy can safely persist.

⚠️ A's stated cost is real — an annotated literal does not show "the full shape at a glance" the way an interface does. If a page genuinely needs the at-a-glance table, say so for that page and propose how, rather than silently degrading the reference.

**Expect this to redden.** PR #6137 proved these types are sealed (`BaseFieldMetadata` has no index signature), so annotating will excess-check every extra key. That is the card working, not a problem — fix what reddens, and ⛔ no `FRAGMENT_MARKER`.

### Verification

- The 26-page table, with the command that produced it.
- After the fix: **diagnostics 0**, **declared fragments unmoved**, blocks-to-compile accounted for (annotating does not change the count; say so).
- **Non-vacuity, executable and specific to this card**: prove a block now **fails** when the documented shape drifts — add a key the exported type does not have, show the gate redden naming it, restore. That is the whole deliverable; without it you have replaced one vacuous block with another.
- ⚠️ Prove the annotation resolves against the **built** `.d.ts` — the gate prints a resolution control line; quote it.
- Docs build; pages still render usefully.

⚠️ **Commit your fix before any ablation whose restore leg is `git checkout`** — it wipes uncommitted work including the fix under test; three devs hit this today. Use `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`, never the bare form. ⛔ Never `git stash`.

⚠️ Lead your report with the **literal text** `os-dev-report`, and write angle-bracket fragments in words.

Refs: #6126 / PR #6137 (where this surfaced) · #5867 · #6121 · #4631.

## Four findings the card did not have, all of which change the work

**1. The conflation is the rule, not the exception — 24 of 26 pages diverge ONLY by widget props.** This is not drift that happened to look like widget props on two pages. It is a consistent authoring convention applied across the whole family: every page documents the metadata keys plus the same three widget props. That consistency is itself evidence the keys were put there deliberately, which strengthens the case against deleting them.

**2. Only two pages carry genuine drift** — keys in neither type:
- `date.mdx` documents `min` / `max`; `DateFieldMetadata` declares **`min_date` / `max_date`**. Its sibling `datetime.mdx` documents `min_date` / `max_date` correctly. Two adjacent reference pages teach two different spellings of the same concept, and one of them does not exist.
- `rich-text.mdx` documents `rows`, `toolbar`, `preview`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight` — five editor-config keys **no shipped type declares**, on either side.

**3. Two pages name a type that does not exist under the derived name.** This matters because it is the gate's own documented false-green mechanism (the `guide/theming` `Theme` case in its header: an annotation that itself errors means the literal underneath is never excess-checked).
- `textarea.mdx` names `TextAreaFieldSchema`; the export is **`TextareaFieldMetadata`** (lowercase `a`). A naming fix.
- `rich-text.mdx` names `RichTextFieldSchema`; **there is no `RichTextFieldMetadata` at all.** The page's own block says `type: 'markdown' | 'html'`, so the honest target is the union `MarkdownFieldMetadata | HtmlFieldMetadata` — both exported. **No new type needs minting for this page**, and it should not be: minting one so the docs become retroactively true is the move this session has refused three times.

**4. Three of the 26 pages are still `plaintext`-fenced** — `auto-number.mdx`, `location.mdx`, `object.mdx` — so they are **not in the compile population at all**. #5867's re-fencing has not reached them. Note the card measured `auto-number` and `object`: the two pages it sampled are among the three the "N blocks now compile" claim never covered.

## What I recommend instead of A or B

The deciding question the card named — "what are these blocks for" — now has a measured answer: **they are serving two readers with one block.** A metadata author (writes `format`, `starting_number`; the literal must survive `@objectstack/spec`'s strict schemas at publish) and a widget author (receives `value`, `onChange`, `className`). Today the single heading serves neither: the metadata author copies `value` / `className` / `disabled` into a field definition and earns a publish-time rejection, and the widget author gets 3 of the 76 props they actually receive.

**Option 2 (recommended) — separate the shapes, and put the widget half in ONE place.**
- `## Field Schema` on each page becomes a literal annotated against the exported `*FieldMetadata` — A's mechanism, which is what makes the gate non-vacuous.
- The widget-prop keys move OUT to a single page documenting `FieldWidgetComponentProps` — which **no** `content/docs/fields` page documents today — linked from each field page.

This keeps A's contract-first property (the second source of truth is deleted, not instrumented) while not deleting real API, and it does not mint 26 copies of one shape.

Rejected alternatives, with reasons:
- **Option 1 — split per page, widget block on all 26.** Same correctness, but it creates 26 copies of one identical shape: a new duplicate to keep honest, which is the thing A exists to avoid.
- **Option 3 — A as written.** Deletes six real exported keys. Ruled out by the measurement.
- **Option 4 — B.** Rejected for the PM's stated reason, and now additionally because a key-set parity checker would report `value`/`className`/`disabled` as drift on all 26 pages when they are not drift. The checker would be wrong on its first run, on every page.

### The four axes

- **Real business need** — measured, not speculative. Both readers exist and both are being misled today; `FieldWidgetComponentProps` has 76 members and zero field-reference pages document it. The only pages that mention it are guides a reader does not land on from the field reference.
- **Long-term soundness** — AGENTS.md #0.1 applied to documentation. One shipped type, one documented location, N links. Option 2 removes the duplicate rather than instrumenting it, and unlike Option 1 it does not create a new one.
- **Making AI-written metadata hard to get wrong** — the strongest axis, and why the conflation matters more than the drift. An AI authoring object metadata reads a heading that says "Field Schema" and copies `value`, `className`, `disabled` into a field definition. Annotating the metadata half against the sealed `*FieldMetadata` makes the page **structurally incapable** of teaching a key the type does not have — the excess-property check does it, not a reviewer.
- **Startup scope discipline** — Option 2 mints no checker, no marker vocabulary, no new export, no new type. It adds one page and 26 links. `rich-text.mdx` resolves against the existing union rather than a new `RichTextFieldMetadata`.

### On A's stated cost, per page

A's "no full shape at a glance" cost is real but **smaller than it looks here**, and I want to be accurate rather than reassuring: these pages already document only a subset — between 11 and 17 exported keys go undocumented on every page (e.g. `LookupFieldMetadata` has 29 keys, the page names 18; `GridFieldMetadata` has 23, the page names 9). The interface was never the full shape at a glance. No page in the set genuinely needs the interface form for a shape it uniquely presents.

---

2. **`date.mdx` `min`/`max`** — fix the docs to `min_date`/`max_date` (the sibling page's spelling, and the shipped one). Confirm this is a docs fix and not a signal the type is wrong.
3. **`rich-text.mdx`'s five editor keys** (`rows`, `toolbar`, `preview`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight`) — they exist in no shipped type. Are they inert prose to delete, or a real widget capability that is undeclared? I did not investigate whether `RichTextField` reads them; that is a different card's question and I did not want to widen scope without a ruling.
4. **The three `plaintext` pages** — re-fence in this card, or leave to #5867's batches? They are the pages the card sampled.

## PM ruling on the four questions + dispatch order — R20, round 2

Ruled by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Same branch: `claude/issue-6138-fields-schema-block-parity`.

⭐ **The stop was correct and the measurement earned it.** The dispatch said to stop if `value` / `className` / `disabled` turned out to be `FieldWidgetComponentProps` members, because the fix would become structural. They are, on 26 of 26 pages, and it is. Implementing option A on that measurement would have deleted six real exported keys across 26 reader-facing pages — the exact failure the stop existed to prevent. Four findings the card did not have came with it.

---

### Q1 — **Option 2**, adopted as recommended

Separate the shapes: `Field Schema` becomes a literal annotated against the exported `*FieldMetadata`, and the widget-prop keys move to **one** page documenting `FieldWidgetComponentProps`.

The reasoning that decides it is the one I used to reject option B on this card: *B adds a checker whose job is to keep a second source of truth honest, while A removes the second source of truth.* Option 2 keeps that property — the annotated literal is checked by the compiler, so the page becomes **structurally incapable** of teaching a key the type lacks — while Option 1 mints 26 copies of one shape, which is a new second source of truth arriving by the fix's own hand. Option 3 is falsified by the measurement. Option 4 was already rejected and the measurement makes it worse: it would report `value`/`className`/`disabled` as drift on all 26 pages when they are not drift — wrong on its first run, on every page.

⚠️ **One binding constraint on the new page, because it is exactly how this fix could recreate the defect it is closing.** `FieldWidgetComponentProps` has **76 members**. ⛔ Do **not** write a prose key-list of 76 members — that is a hand-maintained restatement of a declared surface with nothing judging it, which is **#6086** ("No gate judges prose that restates a declared surface — three docs pages measured wrong about `PageHeaderProps` in one day"), filed against this repo, open. The page must carry an **annotated, gate-compiled** example and name `FieldWidgetComponentProps` as the source of truth, with prose that describes the *categories* of props rather than enumerating them. If a reader needs the full member list, the answer is the type, not a copy of it.

### Q2 — **Fix the docs.** `date.mdx` → `min_date` / `max_date`

Two independent witnesses agree — the shipped `DateFieldMetadata` and the sibling `datetime.mdx` — and one copy diverges. The divergent copy is the wrong one. ⛔ Do not change the type: it would break the sibling page and any producer already on `min_date`.

### Q3 — `rich-text.mdx`'s five editor keys: **separate card, but you determine the answer before filing**

Route it as you recommended, with one addition: ⚠️ **read `RichTextField`'s consumption and file the card with the answer in it.** It is one file. A finding that carries its own measurement is worth many times one that asks a question — and it is the difference between a card triage can grade and a card triage has to re-open. If the widget reads them, that is an undeclared-but-consumed capability and its own defect; if it does not, they are inert prose. Either way the five keys come **out** of the annotated block here, because they would redden it; the filed card decides whether they come **back** as declared members.

### The two wrong names — both fixed here, and one refusal

- `textarea.mdx` names `TextAreaFieldMetadata`; the export is **`TextareaFieldMetadata`**. A typo in a name that must resolve. Fix it.
- `rich-text.mdx` names `RichTextFieldMetadata`, which **does not exist**. Its own block says `type: markdown | html`, so the honest target is the existing `MarkdownFieldMetadata` / `HtmlFieldMetadata` union. ⛔ **Do not mint `RichTextFieldMetadata`** — sixth time this session (#5329, #6107, #6122, #6126, #6135-adjacent). Documentation follows the code; the code does not acquire an export so prose becomes retroactively true.
